chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Be kind to your parents so that your children may be kind to you. Honor the chastity of other men’s women so that they honor the chastity of your women.

key_terms.يَبَرَّكُمْ: They will be kind to you

ai.seo_question: What are the two characteristics that bring reciprocal blessings in family and social relations according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a cosmic reciprocity in social ethics, linking filial piety (*birr al-walidayn*) with marital fidelity. This teaching emphasizes that the moral fabric of the family unit is maintained through mutual respect and modesty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a foundation for spiritual and social harmony.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-75 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn Abdul Jab’bar, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hazrami, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, on the authority of some of his companions that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Be kind to your parents so that your children may be kind to you. Honor the chastity of other men’s women so that they honor the chastity of your women.”
